Eight steps, from an empty folder to an agent running on a public URL. Nothing
here assumes you attended the session.

<div class="resume" data-resume=""></div>

| Step | What you do | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| [1](01-setup/) | Set up — uv, keys, accounts | `/health` returns `ok: true` |
| [2](02-database/) | Create the database | Three tables in Supabase |
| [3](03-tools/) | Write the tools, expose them over MCP | You call them from the Inspector |
| [4](04-manual-loop/) | The agent loop, by hand | It answers from your terminal |
| [5](05-framework/) | The same loop, with a framework | Same answer, a third of the code |
| [6](06-the-wrong-way/) | Wire it up the wrong way | **You get a timeout.** On purpose. |
| [7](07-accept-and-poll/) | Fix it: accept and poll | `202` in 200 ms, steps stream live |
| [8](08-deploy/) | Deploy | A public URL you can send someone |

## Before you start

You need four free accounts and about ten minutes. None of them ask for a card.

| | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Google AI Studio key | [https://aistudio.google.com/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) | the model |
| Supabase project | [https://supabase.com](https://supabase.com) | Postgres + pgvector |
| Render account | [https://render.com](https://render.com) | hosting (step 8 only) |
| GitHub account | [https://github.com](https://github.com) | deploying from a repo |

Plus Python 3.11+ and a code editor.

<Aside type="tip" title="Create your own Gemini key">


Free-tier limits are counted **per key**. If a group shares one, you'll all
rate-limit each other within minutes.

</Aside>

## How the steps work

Each page has the same shape: what you're doing, why, the code, the check that
it worked, and what usually goes wrong. Steps 6 and 7 are a matched pair — 6
builds the bug deliberately so 7 has something to fix.

Your progress is remembered in this browser, so you can stop after any step and
pick it up later.

<Aside type="note" title="You can also just read the finished code">


Everything below already exists in the repo. If you'd rather read than type,
clone it and follow along — the steps tell you which file to open.

</Aside>
